title: Reported Capacity Versus Service Delivery: Health System Resilience in the Provinces Affected by the 2023 Earthquakes in Türkiye
content: Background/Objectives: Health system resilience is often assessed with routine capacity indicators, such as hospital beds, which may not show health planners whether services continued after a shock. We examined whether reported capacity in the 11 provinces of Türkiye’s official disaster area moved with recorded services, the workforce and infant mortality after the February 2023 earthquakes. Methods: In a preregistered difference-in-differences study, we compared these provinces with the other 70 using Ministry of Health yearbooks (2017–2024) and infant mortality data (2017–2025), with wild cluster bootstrap and randomisation inference, Holm adjustment and honest confidence sets. Results: Reported hospital beds changed by 1.4% in 2023–2024 (95% confidence interval [CI] −9.0% to 12.3%). Secondary and tertiary care visits fell by 10.1% (95% CI −17.0% to −2.9%; Holm-adjusted p = 0.040), as did surgical operations and primary care visits; relative to beds, visits fell by 11.3% (95% CI −21.11% to −0.01%). Inpatient admissions fell by 14.7% (95% CI −27.9% to 0.3%; Holm-adjusted p = 0.160). Weighted by population, visits fell by 9.7%, but randomisation inference did not reject this (p = 0.097). Pre-event coefficients for visits and admissions failed a joint test, although none was significant alone; the event-study fall in visits held for post-event departures from parallel trends up to half, but not equal to, the largest pre-event change. Infant mortality rose by 4.65 per 1,000 live births in 2023 (95% CI 1.87 to 7.57), possibly including deaths caused by the earthquakes; in 2024–2025, the estimate was 0.25 (95% CI −0.50 to 0.94), or 0.54 (95% CI 0.09 to 0.98) weighted by births. Conclusions: After a major earthquake, recorded service activity fell relative to the reported bed count. Annual bed counts alone may not show whether services continued; counts of functioning beds and monthly activity data would help.
